subject: Private VPC deployment follow-up: network details & next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-07-08T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private VPC deployment follow-up (post-call recap)

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps: 

Summary of requirements you called out:
- Preferred deployment: Private (VPC) — Finbridge needs network isolation and customer-managed VPC connectivity.
- Connectivity options discussed: AWS PrivateLink vs VPC Peering. You said your Security team prefers PrivateLink but want to validate NAT/egress behavior.
- IP allowlist needs: Finbridge will require a static set of egress IPs or interface endpoints for allowlisting.
- CIDR constraints: your infra team can accept a /28 for the endpoint subnet but needs details.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and encryption at-rest keys (KMS) required.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Please share a point-of-contact for networking (name + preferred time for a short technical call).
2) Provide the VPC CIDR(s) you expect us to peer with and any NAT/firewall rules we should know about.
3) Confirm whether PrivateLink is preferred (we'll need to provision interface endpoints) or if peering is required.

I'll loop in Marissa (solutions engineering) to draft a network checklist and a sample network diagram. If PrivateLink is the path, we'll include required security groups, allowed ports, and expected egress IPs.

Attachments: I can share a baseline network diagram and an SOW draft for review — will attach in follow-up.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finbridge.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-07-09T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment follow-up (post-call recap)

Sean — thanks for the summary and for the quick turnaround. Confirming a few items from our side: 

- Networking POC: Priya Natarajan (priya.natarajan@finbridge.com) — she'll coordinate the tech call and share VPN/VPC details.
- CIDR: Our primary VPC is 10.20.0.0/16; we can carve out a /28 for endpoints if needed.
- PrivateLink preference: Security leans PrivateLink due to no-route-based peering to third-party accounts, but we need to understand egress IP behavior (will calls to your hosted control plane/telemetry go over internet?).
- Firewall: We can update our allowlist once you give the list of interface IPs / egress ranges.
- Compliance: We'll need SOC2 Type II report and confirmation that keys can be managed via our KMS (bring-your-own-key) for model artifacts and logs.

Please share any templates / network diagrams you have. Once Priya is on the thread we can set up a 30-min tech sync.

— Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform, Finbridge Payments
alex.chen@finbridge.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finbridge.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@finbridge.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T11:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment follow-up (post-call recap)

Alex / Priya — looping in the SE side. Attaching a baseline network diagram and a draft SOW to illustrate the PrivateLink option and required network pieces. High level technical checklist below and a few clarifying questions so we can size and scope correctly: 

Technical checklist (PrivateLink path):
- Interface endpoints created in your VPC in a customer-managed subnet (/28 is sufficient for initial interfaces).
- Security groups: allow outbound HTTPS (443) to Redwood interface endpoints; we'll provide precise SG rules.
- Egress / outbound IPs: For outbound calls from your VPC to your users (and to external APIs), the traffic flows normally from your VPC. Calls that must reach Redwood control plane (for metrics, billing, management) will originate from our managed endpoints — we will provide stable private IPs for the interface endpoints (or a list of egress IPs if using NAT).
- SNI/TLS: TLS terminated at our side; mutual TLS not required for initial onboarding (can be added).
- KMS: We support customer-managed keys for data-at-rest; will need cross-account KMS policy details.
- Audit/logging: We'll enable audit log delivery to your CloudWatch (or S3) endpoint per SOW.

Questions for your infra team: 
1) Do you have a preferred subnet and route table for interface endpoints?
2) Any data egress restrictions (e.g., no public egress allowed from control plane)?
3) Who will own DNS entries for the interface endpoints (we can provide recommended names)?

Attaching: network-diagram.pdf, sow-draft.docx (both attached).

If Priya can share 2-3 time slots for a 30-min call next week, I'll bring a solutions engineer and our infra lead. After that call we'll produce a formal network runbook and updated SOW.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference

Attachments: network-diagram.pdf (network diagram, 1 page), sow-draft.docx (SOW v0.2)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment follow-up (post-call recap)

Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick replies. Priya — welcome on the thread. Proposed next steps: 

1) Tech sync: 30-min call to walk the network diagram and confirm PrivateLink vs Peering. Proposed slots: Tue 2026-07-14 10:00am PDT, Tue 2026-07-14 3:00pm PDT, Wed 2026-07-15 11:00am PDT. Please confirm one.
2) Pre-call ask: if you can share the VPC CIDR and confirm whether public egress for control-plane telemetry is allowed, that will speed the call.
3) I added links to the HubSpot deal and a DocuSign placeholder for the SOW so your procurement team can preview terms: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DEAL-2026-0142 and https://www.docusign.com/REDACTED/sign/abc123

I'll schedule the tech sync once you confirm a slot. Marissa will drive the network runbook after the call and update the SOW.

Cheers — Sean
